headline: Quantum state bounds, metrology, and scaled simulations
summary: Today's research spans fundamental quantum metrology, environmental memory diagnostics, deployed entanglement-based QKD networks, and scalable tensor simulation techniques. Together, these papers highlight a continued push toward rigorous performance bounds and practical scalability across quantum information science.

themes.title: Quantum Metrology & Fisher Bounds
themes.body: New techniques establish dimension-independent Fisher information floors using projective designs and constant measurement bases, pushing past traditional limitations in quantum state estimation.

themes.title: Memory, Walks, and Networks
themes.body: Investigations into confined quantum walks reveal boundary-driven stiffness and shape memory, while experimental setups demonstrate genuine three-time quantum memory and a deployed four-city entanglement QKD network.

themes.title: Scalable Quantum Simulation
themes.body: New algorithmic strategies using F2-linear hash partitioning allow scalable Pauli propagation, avoiding synchronization bottlenecks to simulate over ten billion Pauli strings.

connections.body: Both papers address high-dimensional quantum measurement efficiency, with 2611.17288 utilizing projective designs and 2611.17281 investigating a constant number of measurement bases.
